default: No preference on that; use your judgment. If you meant one of the open product decisions, ask about that one thing specifically, naming what it concerns.

answers.answer: A ready hold is kept for 72 hours. Its `expires_at` is the moment it became ready plus 72 hours (it is null while the hold is waiting). From that moment (inclusive) the hold is `expired`, whatever operation looks at it, and it can no longer be collected or cancelled (a Conflict on param `hold`). When it lapses the next in line is offered the book at that same moment: their 72 hours run from then, not from whenever somebody notices, and the same goes down the line.
A member can have at most 3 active holds (waiting or ready) at a time. A fourth is refused with a Conflict on param `member`. Collected, cancelled and expired holds don't count.

Holds are only for books that are not freely available. Placing one on a book that is on the shelf with no hold on it is a Conflict on param `book` (they should just borrow it). A book that is on the shelf only because somebody's hold is ready counts as unavailable, so a hold on it is fine and waits in line.
A member cannot place a hold on a book they currently have on loan, nor on a book they already have an active (waiting or ready) hold on: a Conflict on param `member` in both cases.

A member with any overdue loan can't place a hold: a Conflict on param `member`. A loan is overdue when it is open and now is strictly after its due time (at the due time it is not overdue yet). This is only checked when placing a hold; it does not affect holds already placed, or collecting.
